description: The linothorax was a lightweight cuirass associated especially with Greek hoplites and other infantry, constructed from layered or reinforced textile and often fitted with shoulder flaps and a skirt of pteruges. It offered a useful balance of protection, mobility, and lower weight compared with bronze body armor, and variants remained common in the armies of Macedon and the Hellenistic successor kingdoms. Similar textile or composite cuirasses also appear in Persian service, particularly among troops influenced by Greek and western Anatolian military traditions, where they could be combined with scale elements or other reinforcements.
